subject: MSA/Order Form — inspection window carve-out & SOC2 evidence cadence
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@valencehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Security exhibit questions and request for bounded inspection windows

Priyom —

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. As we start contracting, Valence has two specific asks in the security exhibit and order form that are blockers for procurement:

1) Inspection windows — we can’t support unlimited privileged inspection without a bounded window. Can Redwood accept a 30-day advance notice and a 3–5 business day privileged inspection window for production artifacts (sampled), with scoped objectives?

2) SOC2 / evidence cadence — we usually request continuous access to logs plus quarterly evidence exports. For vendor operational reasons we would accept quarterly snapshots + a SOC2 attestation within 10 business days of request.

3) Pen test language — we need the right to perform or require a third-party pen test once every 12 months. That test must be on a staging environment with controlled data and a mutually-agreed runbook.

I attached our security requirements doc (Valence-SecReqs_v1.docx). If Redwood can propose redlines that map to those asks (or give alternatives), we can move the order form forward.

Can you loop in legal and security ops? We can also do a 30-minute sync tomorrow if helpful.

Best,

Ellen Park
Head of Procurement | Valence Health

Team — forwarding Valence's asks (below). Quick thoughts welcome: we need a defenseable path that preserves our operational controls but is acceptable to procurement. High-level constraints from product/security that I think matter:

- We can provide SOC2 reports and quarterly evidence snapshots; continuous live access to production logs is a non-starter without a contract-specific escrow/monitoring solution.
- For pen tests, we prefer staged runs (staging or synthetic) with a narrow blast radius and least-privileged access.
- Inspection windows for privileged access should be limited (we typically do 3 business days with 30 days notice, escorted access, & scoped artifacts).

Karthik/Olga — can you draft specific redline language for the MSA security exhibit and the order form that I can send back to Ellen? Monica, FYI for handoff if Valence accepts the approach.

If useful, propose two alternatives in the redline: (A) standard inspection + full SOC2 share, (B) bounded inspection + quarterly snapshot + attestation SLA.

Priyom

Priyom / team —

I reviewed Valence's doc and sketched a pragmatic set of redlines we can push back with. High-level summary (redline doc attached):

1) Inspection window carve-out (proposed language):
- Customer may request privileged inspection with >= 30 days' notice.
- Privileged inspection shall be limited to a 5 business day window unless otherwise agreed in writing.
- Redwood will provide scoped artifacts (logs, config snapshots, relevant runbooks) as reasonably necessary for the inspection; production telemetry access will remain read-only and subject to our operational controls.

2) Evidence cadence / SOC2: 
- Redwood will deliver SOC2 Type II reports annually and provide quarterly operational evidence snapshots (redacted where required) upon secure link.
- For on-demand attestation requests, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide supporting evidence within 10 business days.

3) Pen test clause: 
- Customer may commission a penetration test no more than once per 12-month period and only on a mutually-agreed non-production environment.
- Test scope and runbook must be agreed in advance. Redwood will coordinate a single point-of-contact and provide simulated data environments where necessary.

4) Escalation & confidentiality:
- Any sensitive findings will be handled under the MSA's confidentiality and vulnerability disclosure procedures; we propose a 30-day remediation window before public disclosure.

I also suggested two optional concessions that often help procurement accept the deal: a named audit liaison for the inspection and an SLA-backed attestation timeline (e.g., 10 business days for key artifacts) for a premium.

Attachment: security-exhibit-redline_v1.docx (track changes)

Happy to refine — happy to join a call with Valence to walk through the language.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Legal — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear asks and for the doc. We've reviewed internally and attached a proposed redline to the MSA security exhibit and a short amendment to the order form that maps to the Valence requirements. TL;DR of the compromise we are proposing: 

- Inspection windows: 30 days notice + up to 5 business days of privileged inspection; scoped artifacts only; access is read-only and escorted.
- SOC2 & evidence cadence: annual SOC2 Type II share + quarterly operational evidence snapshots via secure link; on-demand attestation turnaround target of 10 business days (commercially reasonable efforts).
- Pen test: permitted once per 12 months on a mutually-agreed non-prod/staging environment; runbook & scope must be agreed at least 15 business days in advance.
